meta.name: Little Bidding Mariáš
meta.blurb: Three-player trick-taking: one secret bid picks a declarer and trump, marriages are announced, and the declarer plays alone against two defenders over 6 deals of 6 tricks.

setup.label: the seating
setup.text: Players are seated P1, P2, P3 (seats 1, 2, 3); seat order is cyclic. Players may not exchange messages at any time.

rules:
CARDS. 20 cards in four suits, Hearts, Bells, Leaves and Acorns, each with ranks A, 10, K, O (Ober) and U (Unter), highest to lowest A, 10, K, O, U. Each Ace and each Ten is worth {ace_points} card points; all other cards are worth 0. Winning the 6th (last) trick of a deal is worth {last_trick_bonus} more, so a deal has {deal_card_points_total} card points in total. Suit order for tie-breaks is Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns.

MATCH. {deals} deals of {tricks_per_deal} tricks each, {total_rounds} rounds; each round is one trick. Players are seated P1, P2, P3 and seat order is cyclic. The eldest is P1 in deals 1 and 4, P2 in deals 2 and 5, P3 in deals 3 and 6. Every score starts at {starting_score}. Players may not exchange messages at any time; defenders cooperate only through their card play.

DEAL. The engine shuffles all 20 cards and deals {hand_size} to each player privately. The remaining {talon_size} cards are the talon: face down, seen by no one, out of play for the whole deal.

BIDDING. Every player privately submits one answer containing a bid and a suit. A bid is PASS or one of {min_bid}, 60, ..., {max_bid} (steps of {bid_step}); a suit is Hearts, Bells, Leaves or Acorns. Any bid not in this list counts as PASS. The eldest may not pass: an eldest PASS or invalid bid counts as {eldest_forced_bid}. A missing or invalid suit becomes the suit in which that player holds the most cards, ties broken by the suit order. All bids and suits are then revealed together. The highest bid wins. If bids are equal, the eldest wins the tie first, then the next player in seat order after the eldest. The winner is the declarer, their bid is the contract T, and their suit is trump. The other two players are the defenders and form a team for this deal.

MARRIAGES. Every player who holds both the K and the O of one suit has a marriage in that suit, worth {trump_marriage_value} in the trump suit and {plain_marriage_value} in any other suit, belonging to its holder's side. The engine publicly announces every marriage, its holder and its value. At the end of the deal a side's marriages count only if that side won at least {min_tricks_for_marriages} trick; if it won none, they do not count.

PLAYING A TRICK. The declarer leads the first trick of the deal; after that the winner of the previous trick leads. Starting with the leader, each player in seat order plays one card, announced to all. The leader may play any card. For the other players: (a) If you hold a card of the led suit, you must play that suit. You must also play one that beats the highest card of the led suit already in the trick, if you can. This beating duty is lifted only when the led suit is not trump and a trump has already been played to this trick. (b) If you hold no card of the led suit but hold a trump, you must play a trump. It must beat the highest trump already in the trick, if you can. (c) Otherwise you may play any card. You are offered only your legal cards. If a player names a card that is illegal or not in their hand, the engine plays for them the legal card of lowest rank; among equal ranks, the first in the suit order. The trick is won by the highest trump in it, or by the highest card of the led suit if it holds no trump (each card's key is its rank + {trump_key_bonus} if trump + {led_suit_key_bonus} if of the led suit; the highest key wins). The card points of the trick, plus {last_trick_bonus} if it is the 6th trick, go to the winner's side: the declarer alone, or the defenders together. The engine announces the trick winner and both sides' running points.

END OF DEAL. 1. The declarer's tally is the declarer's points (including any last-trick bonus), plus the declarer's marriages if the declarer won at least 1 trick, minus the defenders' marriages if the defenders won at least 1 trick. 2. Let S = (T - {contract_offset}) / {contract_divisor}, so 50 gives S = 1 and 150 gives S = 11. 3. If the tally is at least T, the contract is made and S is unchanged; otherwise S becomes -(S + 1). 4. If trump is Hearts, S is multiplied by {hearts_multiplier}. 5. The declarer's score changes by {declarer_score_multiplier} x S, and each defender's score changes by -S. 6. The engine announces the tally, whether the contract was made, and all scores.

WINNING. After round {total_rounds} (6 deals) the player with the highest total score wins; players tied at the top share the win. Every deal is zero-sum.
